title: Strong induction on s+t for the Erdos-Szekeres binomial bound C(s+t, s)
intent: Prove the off-diagonal Ramsey binomial bound HasRamseyProperty (Nat.choose (s+t) s) s t for all s, t by strong induction on the shared measure n = s + t, so the induction step is exactly the pigeonhole recurrence lemma and each base case is monotonicity applied to a zero base case.
also_known_as: generalise-then-induct (the suffices strengthens the statement to one indexed by n)

parent.name: hasRamseyProperty_choose
parent.statement: hasRamseyProperty_choose : ∀ (s t : ℕ), HasRamseyProperty (Nat.choose (s + t) s) s t

children.name: HasRamseyProperty.mono
children.statement: HasRamseyProperty.mono {N N' s t : ℕ} (hNN' : N ≤ N') (h : HasRamseyProperty N s t) : HasRamseyProperty N' s t
children.closed_by: intro m c V hV; exact h c V (hNN'.trans hV)

children.name: hasRamseyProperty_zero_left
children.statement: hasRamseyProperty_zero_left (N t : ℕ) : HasRamseyProperty N 0 t
children.closed_by: refine Or.inl ⟨∅, Finset.empty_subset _, by simp, ?_⟩; the 2-subset condition is vacuous (e ⊆ ∅ forces e = ∅), closed by Finset.subset_empty.mp + simp

children.name: hasRamseyProperty_zero_right
children.statement: hasRamseyProperty_zero_right (N s : ℕ) : HasRamseyProperty N s 0
children.closed_by: refine Or.inr ⟨∅, Finset.empty_subset _, by simp, ?_⟩; symmetric to the left base case, closed by Finset.subset_empty.mp + simp

children.name: HasRamseyProperty.step
children.statement: HasRamseyProperty.step {Ns Nt s t : ℕ} (hs : HasRamseyProperty Ns s (t + 1)) (ht : HasRamseyProperty Nt (s + 1) t) (hNs : 1 ≤ Ns) : HasRamseyProperty (Ns + Nt) (s + 1) (t + 1)
children.closed_by: splits V.erase v into false/true neighbours by card_false_true_split, pigeonholes by le_or_gt Ns R.card, then in each case applies hs or ht and extends the clique by v with mono_insert

applicability.goal_shape: ∀ (s t : ℕ), HasRamseyProperty (Nat.choose (s + t) s) s t: a two-parameter universal statement whose conclusion depends on s and t only through the shared measure s+t and the binomial coefficient C(s+t, s), and whose recurrence lowers s+t by 1
applicability.use_when: the target has a recurrence that lowers a single shared measure (here s+t); the induction should be on that measure, with the two parameters generalised so the induction hypothesis applies at both (s, t+1) and (s+1, t); the base cases and the recurrence step are already stated as separate named lemmas
applicability.avoid_when: the recurrence does not lower one shared measure (a more complex well-founded order is needed), or the strengthened statement indexed by n = s+t is not obviously implied by the target, or there is no monotonicity lemma to move the trivial base value C(n,0) = 1 up to the HasRamseyProperty 1 0 t form the zero base case expects

consequences: The move creates two obligations: (a) the strengthened statement must imply the target, discharged here by instantiating the strengthened theorem at n = s + t; (b) the induction must be well-founded, which Nat.strong_induction_on provides on n. Each match branch must line up its goal with one child's exact statement, so the glue needs the two rewrites Nat.choose_zero_right and Nat.choose_succ_succ (Pascal) to change the target's binomial coefficient into the child's form. Failure modes: if the measure is not a plain sum the generalisation is less obvious, and if the base cases cannot be obtained by monotonicity from a single zero base case, more base-case lemmas are needed.
